question: The Multidimensional Poverty Index of India does NOT consider which of the following for calculating the index?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Environmental quality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is an international measure of acute poverty covering over 100 developing countries.
 
• The MPI uses three dimensions to measure poverty: health, education, and standard of living.
 
• Environmental quality is not considered in the calculation of the MPI.
 
• The MPI was developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Health**

 
 
• This dimension includes indicators such as nutrition and child mortality.
 
• It aims to reflect the ability of individuals to live long and healthy lives.
 
 
 
• **Education**
 
 
• This dimension measures years of schooling and school attendance.
 
• It helps to assess the ability to gain knowledge and skills.
 
 
 
• **Standard of Living**
 
 
• This dimension includes several indicators such as access to electricity, drinking water, sanitation, flooring, cooking fuel, and assets.
 
• It assesses the overall living conditions and quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**
 
 
• The MPI was introduced in 2010 by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It complements traditional income-based poverty measures by capturing the multiple deprivations that people face at the same time.
 
• The MPI is used to measure acute poverty and to identify the poorest of the poor.
 
• It provides a more comprehensive picture of poverty and can help policymakers to target resources and interventions more effectively.
